definition: A synastry conjunction occurs when one person's planet sits at nearly the same degree as the other person's planet — the two energies blend and merge rather than staying separate, intensifying whatever those two planets represent between the pair.
traditional_interpretation: Classically read as the strongest possible synastry contact — a fusing of the two planets' significations, for better or worse depending on which planets are involved and how each is otherwise placed.
modern_interpretation: Modern relationship astrology reads a conjunction as an area where the two people feel almost like one unit — strong instinctive resonance, but also a place where it's easy to lose healthy separateness if the planets involved are already prone to intensity.
psychological_interpretation: Conjunctions often create a felt sense of 'you get me' around that specific theme — powerful bonding, but worth watching for over-identification or codependent patterns if the conjunction involves emotionally loaded planets.
positive_aspects: Deep resonance, instinctive understanding, and a strong felt sense of connection around whatever the two planets represent.
challenges: Can amplify each other's weaknesses in that area as easily as strengths, and can blur healthy boundaries between the two people.
career_meaning: In a business or working relationship, suggests shared instincts and aligned drive around the themes of the planets involved.
relationship_meaning: One of the strongest bonding contacts in synastry — the couple often describes this area as feeling fated or unusually easy to click on.
growth_meaning: Growth here is enjoying the intensity of the merge while still maintaining two distinct, healthy identities rather than losing either person in the other.

definition: A synastry sextile occurs when one person's planet is 60 degrees from the other's — an easy, cooperative angle that opens a genuine opportunity for the two planets' themes to work well together, if both people choose to engage with it.
traditional_interpretation: Classically read as a minor benefic contact — pleasant and helpful, though requiring more conscious effort to activate than the stronger trine.
modern_interpretation: Modern relationship astrology treats a sextile as real, available potential rather than automatic ease — the connection works well when both people actively invest in it, unlike the more effortless trine.
psychological_interpretation: Sextiles often show up as areas where the couple naturally encourages each other's growth — a supportive, low-friction dynamic that rewards engagement.
positive_aspects: Friendly cooperation, mutual encouragement, and an easy foundation to build shared projects or habits on.
challenges: Can go unused if neither person makes the effort to engage with the opportunity it offers — sextiles are potential, not guarantees.
career_meaning: A genuinely helpful contact for collaboration and shared projects when both people put in active effort.
relationship_meaning: A pleasant, easy-to-build-on connection point — good for shared hobbies, communication, or mutual support around the themes involved.
growth_meaning: Growth here is actively using the opportunity this contact offers, rather than assuming the ease will show up without any effort.

definition: A synastry square occurs when one person's planet is 90 degrees from the other's — a friction-generating angle that creates real tension between the two planets' themes, demanding active negotiation rather than offering automatic ease.
traditional_interpretation: Classically read as a challenging, malefic-toned contact — a source of friction, misunderstanding, or conflict between the two people around whatever the planets represent.
modern_interpretation: Modern relationship astrology reframes squares as growth-generating friction rather than pure incompatibility — genuinely difficult, but often the exact contact that pushes both people to develop skills they wouldn't have needed otherwise.
psychological_interpretation: Squares often highlight where each person's unconscious patterns clash — uncomfortable, but frequently the most transformative contact in a chart comparison if both people engage with it consciously rather than avoiding it.
positive_aspects: Real growth potential, dynamic tension that keeps the relationship from becoming stagnant, and the chance to develop genuine skill in an area that doesn't come naturally.
challenges: Recurring friction, misunderstanding, or conflict around the themes of the two planets involved — this contact rarely feels easy.
career_meaning: Can create productive creative tension in a working relationship, or genuine friction if neither person manages it consciously.
relationship_meaning: One of the more challenging synastry contacts — often a recurring source of argument, but also frequently named by long-term couples as where they grew the most.
growth_meaning: Growth here is treating the friction as useful information about a real difference to work through, rather than either avoiding it or treating it as proof of incompatibility.

definition: A synastry trine occurs when one person's planet is 120 degrees from the other's — the easiest, most naturally flowing angle in synastry, letting the two planets' themes support each other with very little friction.
traditional_interpretation: Classically the strongest benefic contact — associated with harmony, ease, and good fortune between the two people wherever it falls.
modern_interpretation: Modern relationship astrology still treats trines as genuinely easy, but adds a caution: because there's so little friction, trines can occasionally lead to complacency or under-appreciating the connection simply because it never demanded effort.
psychological_interpretation: Trines often show up as areas where the couple simply doesn't have to try — a natural, comfortable flow that can be a real source of stability and relief from the effort required elsewhere.
positive_aspects: Effortless harmony, mutual ease, and a genuinely stabilizing, comfortable connection around the themes of the two planets.
challenges: Can be taken for granted or under-invested in precisely because it doesn't demand any active effort to maintain.
career_meaning: A naturally easy, productive working dynamic around the themes involved — often a genuine asset in a business partnership.
relationship_meaning: One of the most comfortable, stabilizing contacts a couple can share — the parts of the relationship that simply feel easy.
growth_meaning: Growth here is actively appreciating and nurturing this ease rather than taking it for granted simply because it requires no effort.

definition: A synastry opposition occurs when one person's planet is 180 degrees from the other's — a magnetic but polarizing angle, where the two planets' themes sit at opposite poles and often play out as complementary differences rather than a shared quality.
traditional_interpretation: Classically read as a tense, challenging contact — associated with conflict and pulling in opposite directions, though also with the strong magnetic attraction that draws two very different people together.
modern_interpretation: Modern relationship astrology reframes oppositions as a mirror or complement — each person often carries what the other is missing, which can be either a powerfully balancing partnership or a recurring source of projection and conflict, depending on self-awareness.
psychological_interpretation: Oppositions frequently show up as attraction to what feels 'other' — the partner can end up carrying a disowned part of oneself, which is either integrated consciously (genuine balance) or fought with unconsciously (recurring conflict).
positive_aspects: Strong magnetic attraction, complementary strengths, and the chance for each person to grow through genuine exposure to a different way of being.
challenges: Polarization, projection, and a tendency to see the difference as a problem with the other person rather than a genuine complementary difference to integrate.
career_meaning: Can create a strong complementary partnership (each covering the other's blind spot) or persistent disagreement, depending on how consciously the difference is handled.
relationship_meaning: One of the most magnetic yet demanding synastry contacts — the 'opposites attract' dynamic, requiring real self-awareness to become a strength rather than a recurring conflict.
growth_meaning: Growth here is recognizing what the other person carries as a genuine complement rather than a threat, and integrating rather than fighting the difference.
